<reason>A won by making the default-rule clash decisive: with no referee, B’s dry-year hold is a renewable stop on Ethiopia’s calendar, i.e. the veto the motion is about. A backed that with hydro non-consumption, Aswan as a real buffer, staged filling without collapse, and one-way “equity.” B landed sharp hits on wet-versus-dry seasons and generation as a motive to hold water, but never specified a non-veto constraint and leaned on a shock that had not arrived.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s turn of B’s “build, but not on a private filling schedule” into “a dam you may build but may not fill is a wall,” then locking it when B said Ethiopia still may not proceed on its remaining timetable while Egypt’s drought objection is live.</best_rebuttal>
